newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom confirms charges structure.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom confirms charges structure.

text.p: France Telecom confirmed on Wednesday it was proposing a price structure for interconnection charges ranging from 0.16 francs to 0.26 francs per minute but rejected comments that the charges were high.

A spokesman for the company said that figures revealed by the Financial Times and Liberation newspapers were correct. But he said a comparison with British Telecom Plc showing the British charges were much cheaper was incorrect because the British prices were not "all in" like the French.
Britain has the lowest interconnection rates in Europe.
France Telecom is proposing a charge of 0.16 francs per minute for a local operator zone of up to 220,000 subscribers.
This would be a charge for a local operator, rival to France Telecom, which needs to use the France Telecom network for connections within a local zone.
The law also permits this local operator to put up its own infrastructure or use another network than France Telecom's.
The comparable British price is 0.09 francs per minute, but BT also charges an amount for the further development of the network.
A second price band, of 0.18 francs per minute, would apply for the cost of regional calls from one operator to another, which stands at 0.19 francs in Britain.
National calls would be charged at 0.26 francs per minute, the same as the British level.
These are prices that France Telecom, as the traditional operator, would charge to other operators. They are not the call rates for consumers and businesses.

The prices are included in a document that French Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon has sent to potential future telecoms competitors to France Telecom for their comments before November 30.
The minister plans to issue a decree in early 1997 fixing the price list so that the interconnection prices will be known before the first tranche of shares in France Telecom are set to be sold.
Neither in Germany, where Deutsche Telekom was listed on the share market on Monday, nor in Italy which is preparing STET for sale, have the interconnection charges been fixed.
